rationale: Both ground-truth threads (validation-section completeness, Ref2VA testing status) are already resolved in the diff shown, so neither candidate scores high recall, but Y engages more substantively with Ref2VA readiness (download-pattern prerequisite for the restart command, OOM risk on the untested profile) which is conceptually closest to the human reviewer's 'have you tested ref2va' concern, while X only touches it via an unrelated audio_reference formatting nit. Both are well-grounded and precise, citing specific file/line evidence and code paths, but Y's major finding — that text-encoder-tp-size scales in lockstep with Ulysses degree across the sweep, making the published memory-model fit unidentifiable and cross-validating an alternate 44.2 GiB encoder-size reading against MiniMax-H3.md's documented ~48 GiB — is a substantially deeper and more consequential correctness catch than anything in X's review. Y's sheer volume includes some marginal nitpicks (HBM vs GDDR7 terminology, 96 vs 95.6 GiB precision) that slightly dilute average precision, but its actionable code-snippet fixes and broader, better-substantiated coverage still edge out X's more concise but shallower set of findings.
